newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia port strike blocks 27,000 T sugar.
newsitem.headline: Colombia port strike blocks 27,000 T sugar.

text.p: The six-day-old dock workers' strike in Colombia's main Pacific coast port has paralyzed the export of at least 27,000 tonnes of sugar, a port official said Monday.
The official, in charge of storage operations at port of Buenaventura, said 17,000 tonnes was bulk sugar in containers together with another 10,000 tonnes in 200,000 50-kg sacks.

The final figure could be much higher, but port officials were unable to give a figure of the amount of sugar loaded on to trucks that have been waiting in and around the port since the strike was declared late Tuesday.

Officials of National Coffee Growers' Federation said last week that 160,000 60-kg bags of coffee had been snarled in the industrial action. The port official said Monday that about 60,000 60-kg bags were in warehouses at dockside and the remainder was on trucks.
The official said 1,800 containers had been blocked by the strike and at least 70,000 tonnes of cargo, in warehouses and already loaded into containers, was paralyzed.

Six ships are currently moored at quayside in Buenaventura with another six anchored and waiting to dock. Since the start of the industrial action at least 12 vessels have been diverted to Colombia's Caribbean coastal ports via Balboa in Panama or have docked in Guayaquil, Ecuador.

It is estimated Buenaventura port is losing about $500,000 for every day of the strike. Dock workers are pressing for higher wages, sickness and injury benefits and changes in the way they are contracted.
Talks between union representatives, cargo handling operators, ship owners and the port superintendent began in Buenaventura at 0900 local/1400 GMT Monday in a bid to break the deadlock.

Representatives of the dock workers' union SINTRAMARITIMOS were due to meet regional heads of the Unitary Workers' Confederation (CUT), the labor federation to which the dockers are affiliated, in Cali later in the day.
More top-level talks are planned for 0900 local Tuesday in Bogota and will include officials from the Labor and Transport Ministries.
